In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

aggrecan molecules are very important to the mechanical behavior of cartilage, and the shear behavior of aggrecan molecules depends on bath IS, lateral displacement rate, probe tip size and shape, and compressive force.

the lateral nanomechanics and lateral nanotribology of aggrecan are both complex and dependent on the experimental conditions, including bath IS, lateral displacement rate, and the end-radii of the probe tip.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the brush-like aggrecan layer in cartilage is a highly compressible and deformable structure that exhibits both elastic and nonelastic behavior in aqueous NaC1 solutions.
aggrecan macropolymers are capable of resisting large shear strains and that the shear resistance is sensitive to both the bath IS and rate.

aggrecan molecules are highly compressed in cartilage, and that the lateral resistance to shear deformation is dominated by the brush-like aggrecan molecules in the superficial zone of the tissue, where they are highly concentrated and oriented parallel to the surface.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the lateral force of aggrecan monolayer is dominated by the electrostatic interaction between aggrecan macroradicals and that the electrostatic interaction is affected by bath IS, compressive strain, and lateral displacement rate.
aggrecan is a highly compressible and viscoelastic macromolecule that can be compressed by up to 50-60% at physiological IS and can exhibit a significant amount of viscoelasticity at high IS.
